sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是“99%隐形”。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: After World War I, in Frankfurt, Germany, the city government was taking on a big project.
sentences.zh: 第一次世界大战后，在德国法兰克福，市政府正在开展一项宏大的工程。

sentences.en: A lot of residents were in dire straits, and in the second half of the 1920s,
sentences.zh: 许多居民当时生活在水深火热之中，在二十世纪二十年代的后半叶，

sentences.en: the city built over 10,000 public housing units.
sentences.zh: 该市建造了超过一万套公共住房。

sentences.en: It was some of the earliest modern architecture, simple, clean, and uniform.
sentences.zh: 这是最早的一些现代建筑，简单、干净而又统一。

sentences.en: The massive housing effort was, in many ways, eye-poppingly impressive,
sentences.zh: 在许多方面，这项大规模的住房建设工程令人惊叹不已，

sentences.en: with all new construction and sleek, cutting-edge architecture.
sentences.zh: 它拥有全新的建筑外观以及时尚前沿的建筑风格。

sentences.en: But one room in these new housing units was far and away the most lauded and influential,
sentences.zh: 但在这些新住宅中，有一个房间毫无疑问是备受赞誉且最具影响力的，

sentences.en: and that was the kitchen.
sentences.zh: 那就是厨房。

sentences.en: That's reporter and friend of the show, Katie Thornton.
sentences.zh: 说话的是记者兼本节目之友凯蒂·桑顿。

sentences.en: Many consider this room, which has come to be known as the Frankfurt Kitchen,
sentences.zh: 许多人认为这个后来被称为“法兰克福厨房”的房间，

sentences.en: to be nothing less than the first modern kitchen.
sentences.zh: 堪称名副其实的第一个现代厨房。

sentences.en: And looking at it today is a real trip,
sentences.zh: 今天看着它真是一种奇妙的体验，

sentences.en: because you'd be forgiven for thinking that you're looking at an IKEA display.
sentences.zh: 因为你会觉得自己是在看一个宜家展厅，这也情有可原。

sentences.en: It's tidy, practical, and simple.
sentences.zh: 它整洁、实用而又简朴。

sentences.en: Okay, shall we?
sentences.zh: 好了，我们要开始了吗？

sentences.en: We shall.
sentences.zh: 开始吧。

sentences.en: A handful of these original Frankfurt kitchens still exist, mostly in museums,
sentences.zh: 这些最初的法兰克福厨房仍有一些存世，大多在博物馆里，

sentences.en: and Katie went to check out one at MIA, the Minneapolis Institute of Art.
sentences.zh: 凯蒂去明尼阿波利斯艺术博物馆（MIA）参观了其中一个。

sentences.en: Okay, watch your step.
sentences.zh: 好了，请注意脚下。

sentences.en: Thanks.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Jennifer Komar Olivares, head of exhibition planning and strategy at the museum,
sentences.zh: 明尼阿波利斯艺术博物馆展览规划与战略负责人詹妮弗·科马尔·奥利瓦雷斯，
zh_words: 詹妮弗·科马尔·奥利瓦雷斯

sentences.en: led me over the stanchion and into this room to see it firsthand.
sentences.zh: 带我跨过护栏走进这个房间，近距离观察它。

sentences.en: And it's honestly kind of strange to see it in a museum,
sentences.zh: 老实说，在博物馆里看到它感觉有点奇怪，

sentences.en: because to our modern eyes, it doesn't appear to be high art.
sentences.zh: 因为以我们的现代眼光来看，它似乎算不上什么高级艺术。

sentences.en: So coming in is the electric cooker.
sentences.zh: 迎面走来的是电磁炉。

sentences.en: It just looks like a kitchen.
sentences.zh: 它看起来就像个普通的厨房。

sentences.en: And it has two burners on the top, one large one and one small one.
sentences.zh: 它的顶部有两个炉盘，一个大的和一个小的。

sentences.en: It may look ordinary, but many of the things that are now standard kitchen features
sentences.zh: 它看起来或许很普通，但在法兰克福厨房出现之前，如今许多标准的厨房功能

sentences.en: were pretty unheard of before the Frankfurt Kitchen.
sentences.zh: 在当时可以说是闻所未闻。

sentences.en: Things like a modern stove.
sentences.zh: 比如现代化的炉灶。

sentences.en: So, wow.
sentences.zh: 哇哦。

sentences.en: I'm sure it was transformative.
sentences.zh: 我敢说它具有颠覆性的意义。

sentences.en: And well-planned storage to stash your plates and glasses.
sentences.zh: 还有规划合理的储物空间，用来存放盘子和玻璃杯。

sentences.en: These, I think, are for pot storage.
sentences.zh: 我想这些是用来放锅的。

sentences.en: And a way to wash dishes that didn't involve hauling a heavy tub of water into the house.
sentences.zh: 以及一种洗碗的方式，不再需要费力把沉重的水桶提进屋里。

sentences.en: It's a double sink.
sentences.zh: 这是一个双槽水槽。

sentences.en: And racks for drying those dishes.
sentences.zh: 还有用来烘干这些餐具的沥水架。

sentences.en: The idea is to have them dry off the counter to free up the counter space for other things.
sentences.zh: 其理念是让它们在台面上风干，从而腾出台面空间来做其他事情。

sentences.en: Even the countertops themselves were revolutionary.
sentences.zh: 甚至连台面本身都是革命性的。

sentences.en: Because before this, there weren't long, continuous surfaces that were uniform in height.
sentences.zh: 因为在此之前，并没有高度统一的长条形连续台面。

sentences.en: Most kitchens just had whatever random assortment of tables you could throw in them.
sentences.zh: 大多数厨房只有你能塞进去的各种随机拼凑的桌子。

sentences.en: And my back aches just thinking about hunching over their variable heights while prepping food.
sentences.zh: 一想到要在那些高度不一的台面上弯腰准备食物，我的背就隐隐作痛。

sentences.en: The Frankfurt Kitchen now appears so commonplace that it's difficult to comprehend
sentences.zh: 如今，法兰克福厨房看起来是如此寻常，以至于人们很难理解

sentences.en: just how groundbreaking it was when it was first designed.
sentences.zh: 它最初被设计出来时是多么具有开创性。

sentences.en: And that's all thanks to a woman named Margareta Schüter-Lahatzky.
sentences.zh: 这一切都要归功于一位名叫玛格丽特·舒特-拉哈茨克的女性。

sentences.en: Born in 1897 in Austria, Schüter-Lahatzky was one of the country's first woman architects.
sentences.zh: 舒特-拉哈茨克于1897年出生于奥地利，是该国最早的女建筑师之一。

sentences.en: And early in her career, she started designing for people who had never been designed for on a large scale.
sentences.zh: 在其职业生涯的早期，她开始为那些从未在宏大叙事中被考虑过的人群进行设计。

sentences.en: Especially women, who were often saddled with childcare, laundry, and cooking.
sentences.zh: 尤其是那些常常被育儿、洗衣和做饭压得喘不过气来的女性。

sentences.en: She brought that same approach to the Frankfurt Kitchen.
sentences.zh: 她将这种同样的理念带到了法兰克福厨房的设计中。

sentences.en: She wanted it to be a streamlined space that made cooking less burdensome and faster.
sentences.zh: 她希望这是一个精简的空间，能让烹饪变得不那么繁重且更加高效。

sentences.en: So women could get it done and then pursue lives and jobs outside of the home.
sentences.zh: 这样女性就能快点搞定，然后去追求家庭之外的生活和工作。

sentences.en: It was a feminist kitchen, made with the needs of women in mind.
sentences.zh: 这是一个女权主义厨房，专为满足女性的需求而打造。

sentences.en: But Schüter-Lahatzky wasn't actually the first to tackle the problem of the home kitchen.
sentences.zh: 但舒特-拉哈茨克其实并不是第一个着手解决家庭厨房问题的人。

sentences.en: A space fraught with complications for a lot of women.
sentences.zh: 对许多女性来说，这是一个充满种种复杂难题的空间。

sentences.en: In fact, by the time Schüter-Lahatzky designed the Frankfurt Kitchen,
sentences.zh: 事实上，早在舒特-拉哈茨克设计法兰克福厨房之前，

sentences.en: many feminists had already been questioning whether private kitchens could ever be designed to liberate women.
sentences.zh: 许多女权主义者就已经在质疑，私人厨房是否真的能够被设计成将女性解放出来的场所。

sentences.en: Or whether the kitchen itself was irredeemable and just needed to be abolished.
sentences.zh: 还是说厨房本身无可救药，唯有彻底废除这一途。

sentences.en: For much of modern history, in most cultures,
sentences.zh: 在现代历史的大部分时间里，在大多数文化中，

sentences.en: kitchens were the realm of women and of servants who worked in the home.
sentences.zh: 厨房都是女性和家中仆人操持的领域。

sentences.en: And those spaces weren't considered worthy of an architect's expertise.
sentences.zh: 而这些空间并不被认为配得上建筑师的专业专长。

sentences.en: For the most part, it's very difficult in publications of architecture to ever find plans, photographs of kitchens.
sentences.zh: 在很大程度上，在建筑出版物中极难找到厨房的平面图或照片。

sentences.en: You'd see beautiful images of living rooms, even sometimes bedrooms, and just very few kitchens.
sentences.zh: 你会看到客厅的美丽图片，有时甚至是卧室，却极少看到厨房。

sentences.en: This is Mary McLeod.
sentences.zh: 这位是玛丽·麦克劳德。

sentences.en: She teaches at Columbia University's Graduate School of Architecture and Planning.
sentences.zh: 她在哥伦比亚大学建筑与规划研究生院任教。

sentences.en: And she says what we do know about kitchens prior to the 20th century,
sentences.zh: 她表示，我们所了解的20世纪之前的厨房，

sentences.en: at least in Europe and America, is that they were really unpleasant.
sentences.zh: 至少在欧洲和美洲，确实是非常糟糕的。

sentences.en: They're hodgepodges.
sentences.zh: 它们杂乱无章。

sentences.en: They're full of objects with no order.
sentences.zh: 里面塞满了毫无秩序的物件。

sentences.en: It was smoky.
sentences.zh: 里面烟雾缭绕。

sentences.en: They were really unconscionable conditions with very little air circulation or light.
sentences.zh: 那里的条件简直惨不忍睹，几乎没有什么空气流通或光线。

sentences.en: One American feminist from the 19th century wrote of
sentences.zh: 一位19世纪的美国女权主义者曾这样写道：

sentences.en: roasted ladies, scorched and sooty from preparing meals day in and day out.
sentences.zh: 日复一日地准备饭菜，让妇人们像烤肉一样被熏得焦黑、满身烟灰。

sentences.en: Remember, this was before restaurants were common or affordable in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 记住，这发生在餐馆在美国尚未普及或人们还消费不起的时期。

sentences.en: and much of Europe.
sentences.zh: 以及欧洲的大部分地区。

sentences.en: No fast, easy, cheap, prepared food.
sentences.zh: 没有快捷、简便、廉价的预制食品。

sentences.en: So on top of raising children, plus hand-washing and drying laundry,
sentences.zh: 因此，除了抚养孩子，加上手洗和晾晒衣物，

sentences.en: and sometimes juggling factory jobs outside the home,
sentences.zh: 有时还要兼顾家门外的工厂工作，

sentences.en: preparing the 1,095 meals a year for the family was regarded as absolute drudgery by many women.
sentences.zh: 对于许多女性来说，每年为家庭准备1,095顿饭被视为绝对的苦差事。

sentences.en: Absolute drudgery that was also unpaid.
sentences.zh: 这是一项没有任何报酬的绝对苦差事。

sentences.en: And in the years after the Civil War, a number of American feminists started to argue that
sentences.zh: 在南北战争结束后的几年里，一些美国女权主义者开始提出，

sentences.en: uncompensated housework was keeping women financially and intellectually oppressed.
sentences.zh: 无偿的家务劳动使女性在经济和智力上受到压迫。

sentences.en: And one of the ways they thought they could change that was through urban design.
sentences.zh: 她们认为改变这种状况的方法之一就是通过城市规划。

sentences.en: In the period right after the Civil War, they were debating whether or not there were new ways
sentences.zh: 在南北战争结束后的时期，她们一直在争论是否存在新的方式

sentences.en: to organize housing that would eliminate women's unpaid labor.
sentences.zh: 来组织能够消除女性无偿劳动的住房。

sentences.en: Dolores Hayden is a trailblazing architectural historian and professor emerita at Yale.
sentences.zh: 多洛雷斯·海登是耶鲁大学的开创性建筑历史学家兼荣誉退休教授。

sentences.en: She says that some feminists thought you could design your way out of unpaid housework
sentences.zh: 她表示，一些女权主义者认为，你可以通过将所谓的家务劳动

sentences.en: by removing so-called housework from houses.
sentences.zh: 从房屋中移除，来用设计摆脱无偿家务。

sentences.en: And in the U.S., one of the early activists who called for this kind of design solution
sentences.zh: 在美国，呼吁这种设计解决方案的早期活动家之一

sentences.en: was a writer and organizer named Melissina Faye Peirce.
sentences.zh: 是一位名叫梅丽西娜·费伊·皮尔斯的作家兼组织者。

sentences.en: And Melissina Peirce was particularly clear that women should not be expected to render
sentences.zh: 梅丽西娜·皮尔斯特别明确地指出，不应该期望女性

sentences.en: unpaid services to the men and children in their households,
sentences.zh: 向家里的男人和孩子提供无偿服务，

sentences.en: but that they should receive some economic compensation for their labors.
sentences.zh: 而是她们的劳动应该获得一些经济补偿。

sentences.en: And what she proposed was the former Producers' Co-op of Housewives in 1868 in Cambridge, Massachusetts.
sentences.zh: 她提出的建议是1868年在马萨诸塞州剑桥市成立的前身家庭主妇生产者合作社。

sentences.en: Peirce started the Cambridge Cooperative Housekeeping Society,
sentences.zh: 皮尔斯创办了剑桥合作家务协会，

sentences.en: and it operated out of a big building near Harvard Square.
sentences.zh: 它在哈佛广场附近的一栋大楼里运作。

sentences.en: The co-op employed women who were paid to do laundry and bake bread for nearby families,
sentences.zh: 该合作社雇用了女性，她们获得报酬为附近的家庭洗衣服和烤面包，

sentences.en: tasks most women had to do on their own and without pay.
sentences.zh: 这些任务原本是大多数女性不得不独自完成且没有报酬的。

sentences.en: Producers' cooperatives, where workers would pool much of their labor and their power,
sentences.zh: 生产者合作社很常见，工人们会在其中汇集大部分劳动和力量。

sentences.en: were common.
sentences.zh: 但皮尔斯的合作社是第一个承担家务劳动的。

sentences.en: But Peirce's was the first to take on housework.
sentences.zh: 因此，她激怒了那些认为女性不应该为本应出于爱和义务而做的工作要求报酬的人。

sentences.en: So she infuriated people who thought that women shouldn't be asking for pay
sentences.zh: 皮尔斯的合作社持续了大约两年，这已经是一个壮举了。

sentences.en: for the work they should be doing out of love and obligation.
sentences.zh: 但她从未实现自己更大的愿景，

sentences.en: Peirce's co-op lasted for about two years, which is a feat.
sentences.zh: 那就是将家务合作社融入新住房项目的设计中。

sentences.en: But she never achieved her bigger vision,
sentences.zh: 她想象过带有集体厨房和洗衣房的大型公寓楼。

sentences.en: which was to integrate housework cooperatives into the designs of new housing projects.
sentences.zh: 但其他女权主义者也开始对所谓的家务劳动应该从家庭中移除这个想法产生兴趣。

sentences.en: She imagined big apartment blocks with collective kitchens and laundry.
sentences.zh: 其中一位是玛丽·豪兰，她曾是一名纺织工人，后来转行成为建筑师，

sentences.en: But other feminists were also getting interested in this idea that
sentences.zh: 她受到自己在法国吉斯度过了一年的一个合作社区的启发。

sentences.en: so-called housework should be removed from the home.
sentences.zh: 该社区被称为“社会宫”。

sentences.en: One of them was Marie Howland, a textile worker turned architect,
sentences.zh: 社会宫围绕着一座铸铁厂建造，

sentences.en: who was inspired by a cooperative community she spent a year at in Guise, France.
sentences.zh: 那里的居民轮流参与共享家务计划，

sentences.en: It was known as the Social Palace.
sentences.zh: 其中包括为350名钢铁工人和他们的家人提供预制食品服务。

sentences.en: The Social Palace was built around an iron foundry,
sentences.zh: 当豪兰研究这个社区的设计时，

sentences.en: and the residents there took turns in a shared housekeeping program,
sentences.zh: 她开始构想自己的乌托邦社会，

sentences.en: which included a prepared food service for the 350 iron workers and their families.
sentences.zh: 在那里，像社会宫这样的地方成为了常态。

sentences.en: And as Howland studied the design of the community,
sentences.zh: 当她回到美国后，她写了一部关于这方面的小说。

sentences.en: she began to dream up her own utopian society,
sentences.zh: 玛丽·豪兰并不是唯一一个用小说来构想充满无厨房房屋的理想未来的人。

sentences.en: where a place like the Social Palace was the norm.
sentences.zh: 许多人都在写科幻小说，

sentences.en: And she wrote a novel about it when she came back to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 其中包括一些描绘带有共享合作厨房的女权主义未来的书籍。

sentences.en: Marie Howland wasn't the only person using fiction to dream up an ideal future
sentences.zh: 这种充满可能性的感觉是显而易见的。

sentences.en: full of kitchen-less houses.
sentences.zh: 而且不仅仅是女性在写这些。

sentences.en: A lot of people were writing futuristic novels,
sentences.zh: 我惊讶地发现，有很多男性也在写关于通过新住房和新基础设施实现女性解放的小说。

sentences.en: including some books that depicted a feminist future with shared cooperative kitchens.
sentences.zh: 其中一些小说让所有人都住在高层建筑里。

sentences.en: The sense of possibility was palpable.
sentences.zh: 另一个人则让所有人在一个女权主义星球——火星上生活。

sentences.en: And it wasn't only that women were writing them.
sentences.zh: 在通俗小说和一些现实世界的实验之间，无厨房房屋的概念正在传播开来。

sentences.en: I was surprised how much I found men were writing these novels about women's liberation
sentences.zh: 1874年，玛丽·豪兰看到了实现其中一些想法的机会。

sentences.en: through new housing and new infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 她开始与两名男性设计师阿尔伯特·金西·欧文和约翰·迪里合作。

sentences.en: Some of them had everyone living in high-rise buildings.
sentences.zh: 他们是当时美国众多相信一个更加和谐的社会是可能的人之一，

sentences.en: Another person sighted everyone on a feminist planet, Mars.
sentences.zh: 在那个社会里，人们集体生活并共同拥有所有生产资料。

sentences.en: Between popular fiction and a few real-world experiments,
sentences.zh: 在19世纪70年代，他们与玛丽·豪兰一起着手建设一个完美的城镇。

sentences.en: the concept of a kitchen-less house was spreading.
sentences.zh: 他们在铁路尽头宣传墨西哥的一个新镇。

sentences.en: And in 1874, Marie Howland saw her chance to implement some of those ideas.
sentences.zh: 这个城镇名叫托波洛博姆波，最初他们的设计只有带厨房的单户住宅。

sentences.en: She started working with two men, designers Albert Kimsey Owen and John Deary.
sentences.zh: 但玛丽·豪兰说服他们在图纸上画入了一小群无厨房的房屋，

sentences.en: They were among the many people in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 每栋房子都可以使用一个共享厨房，居民们会在那里轮流工作。

sentences.en: at the time who believed that a more harmonious society
sentences.zh: 他们有详尽的计划。

sentences.en: was possible, one where people lived collectively and jointly owned all means of production.
sentences.zh: 他们花了很多钱来绘制这些计划并宣传这些计划，

sentences.en: And in the 1870s, together with Marie Howland, they set out to build a perfect town.
sentences.zh: 因此很多人都听说了托波洛博姆波。

sentences.en: They were promoting a new town in Mexico at the end of a railroad line.
sentences.zh: 但并没有很多人真正住进托波洛博姆波。

sentences.en: The town was called Topolobompo, and originally their designs just had single-family homes with kitchens.
sentences.zh: 这个项目资金很快就耗尽了，甚至在豪兰的无厨房房屋建造之前就没钱了。

sentences.en: But Marie Howland convinced them to sketch in small groups of kitchen-free houses,
sentences.zh: 对男性创始人来说，那些并不是首要任务。

sentences.en: each with access to a shared kitchen, where residents would take turns working.
sentences.zh: 但梦想并没有结束。

sentences.en: They had elaborate plans.
sentences.zh: 1915年，另一位名叫爱丽丝·康斯坦斯·奥斯汀的女权主义者
zh_words: 爱丽丝·康斯坦斯·奥斯汀

sentences.en: They spent a lot of money drawing up these plans and publicizing the plans,
sentences.zh: 开始了她的宏伟构想。

sentences.en: so a lot of people heard about Topolobompo.
sentences.zh: 这是一个充满创新精神的时代。

sentences.en: But not a lot of people got to live at Topolobompo.
sentences.zh: 尽管阻力重重，她们依然砥砺前行。

sentences.en: The project ran out of money pretty quickly, before Howland's kitchen-less houses could even be built.
sentences.zh: 历史往往由这些不凡的构想所重塑。

sentences.en: To the male founders, those weren't a priority.
sentences.zh: 她们的努力为后世奠定了坚实的基础。

sentences.en: But the dream wasn't over.
sentences.zh: 这些先驱者的精神至今仍然闪烁着光芒。

sentences.en: In 1915, another feminist named Alice Constance Austin
sentences.zh: 她们的名字将被永远铭记在建筑与社会变革的历史中。

sentences.en: embarked on another kitchen-less utopian experiment.
sentences.zh: 开启了又一场没有厨房的乌托邦实验。

sentences.en: Together with Jobe Harriman, a socialist politician,
sentences.zh: 她与社会主义政治家乔布·哈里曼合作，

sentences.en: she set out to create a community called Llano del Rio, outside L.A.
sentences.zh: 着手在洛杉矶郊外创建名为“里奥拉诺”的社区。

sentences.en: She thought it could be a city of kitchen-less houses,
sentences.zh: 她认为这可以是一个没有厨房的住宅城市，

sentences.en: and she thought that the food could come through some underground tunnels by trains.
sentences.zh: 并且她认为食物可以通过一些地下隧道由火车运送过来。

sentences.en: Oh, right.
sentences.zh: 哦，对。

sentences.en: Food trains.
sentences.zh: 食物列车。

sentences.en: Now we're talking.
sentences.zh: 这话说得对。

sentences.en: Not railroad trains, but lines that would carry the food from a central kitchen to each house
sentences.zh: 不是铁路列车，而是将食物从中央厨房运送到每栋房屋的输送线，

sentences.en: and would take away the dirty dishes.
sentences.zh: 还能顺便把脏盘子收走。

sentences.en: Austin drew maps upon maps and tons of floor plans.
sentences.zh: 奥斯汀绘制了大量的地图和无数的平面图。

sentences.en: She published her ideas in the journal out of Llano del Rio, the Western Comrade,
sentences.zh: 她在里奥拉诺的期刊《西方同志》上发表了自己的想法，

sentences.en: and even applied to patent her underground food train idea.
sentences.zh: 甚至申请了地下食物列车创意的专利。

sentences.en: But like Topolobompo, Llano del Rio also struggled to get enough funding.
sentences.zh: 但就像托波洛班波一样，里奥拉诺也难以获得充足的资金。

sentences.en: The male founders weren't that into the idea of the kitchen-less houses,
sentences.zh: 男创始人们对没有厨房的房屋这个想法并不太感兴趣，

sentences.en: and the community fell apart before they could ever be constructed.
sentences.zh: 结果社区在这些房子建成之前就解散了。

sentences.en: But the kitchen-less house movement still didn't die.
sentences.zh: 但无厨房住宅运动并没有就此消亡。

sentences.en: Around the same era, in England, the urban planner Ebenezer Howard
sentences.zh: 大约在同一时期，在英国，城市规划师埃比尼泽·霍华德

sentences.en: actually incorporated kitchen-less homes into some of his garden city communities.
sentences.zh: 实际上将无厨房住宅纳入了他的一些田园城市社区中。

sentences.en: He called these complexes cooperative quadrangles.
sentences.zh: 他将这些综合体称为合作方庭。

sentences.en: They had a shared courtyard and shared kitchen,
sentences.zh: 它们拥有共享的庭院和共享的厨房，

sentences.en: surrounded by smaller kitchen-less dwellings.
sentences.zh: 周围环绕着较小的无厨房住宅。

sentences.en: He thought that they would be perfect for single women who were working
sentences.zh: 他认为这些非常适合工作的单身女性，

sentences.en: or for couples who didn't want to run an elaborate domestic establishment.
sentences.zh: 或者不想操持繁琐家务的夫妇。

sentences.en: And he and his wife lived in one of them.
sentences.zh: 他和妻子就住在其中一处。

sentences.en: By the late 19-teens in the U.S.,
sentences.zh: 到美国1910年代末期，

sentences.en: the idea of ending the private kitchen was pretty mainstream.
sentences.zh: 废除私人厨房的想法已经相当主流。

sentences.en: Big publications, including Ladies Home Journal,
sentences.zh: 各大出版物，包括《女性家庭杂志》，

sentences.en: a magazine whose very title literally puts women in the home,
sentences.zh: 一本连名字都字面意思把女性限定在家里的杂志，

sentences.en: ran articles promoting kitchen-less houses.
sentences.zh: 都发表了推广无厨房住宅的文章。

sentences.en: They compared the private kitchen to the private spinning wheel,
sentences.zh: 他们将私人厨房比作私人纺织车，

sentences.en: a relic of the past and a manifestation of oppressive, unpaid labor
sentences.zh: 这是过去的遗迹，也是压迫性、无报酬劳动的体现，

sentences.en: that could be done much better on a larger scale.
sentences.zh: 而这种劳动完全可以更大规模地做得更好。

sentences.en: It was a popular and progressive movement,
sentences.zh: 这是一场受欢迎且富有进步意义的运动，

sentences.en: but it certainly wasn't without flaws.
sentences.zh: 但它当然也并非没有缺陷。

sentences.en: Many of these utopian movements were led by middle-class white women
sentences.zh: 许多这类乌托邦运动由中产阶级白人女性领导，

sentences.en: who didn't appear to seriously embrace the needs and contributions
sentences.zh: 她们似乎并没有认真接纳黑人女性和有色人种女性的

sentences.en: of black women and women of color.
sentences.zh: 需求与贡献。

sentences.en: Many of these women had been violently forced
sentences.zh: 其中许多女性几代人以来一直遭受暴力强制，

sentences.en: into caretaking and housekeeping roles for generations
sentences.zh: 通过奴隶制和契约劳役沦为

sentences.en: through slavery and indentured servitude.
sentences.zh: 照顾者和家政服务角色。

sentences.en: And they were also fighting their own battles for dignity and pay.
sentences.zh: 她们也在为自身的尊严和报酬进行着抗争。

sentences.en: In time, the movement for kitchen-less houses faced roadblocks
sentences.zh: 随着时间推移，无厨房住宅运动遇到了

sentences.en: it couldn't overcome.
sentences.zh: 无法克服的重重障碍。

sentences.en: Inflation hit hard after World War I,
sentences.zh: 一战后通货膨胀严重冲击，

sentences.en: and people were struggling.
sentences.zh: 人们生活艰难。

sentences.en: Figuring out how to pay for prepared meals
sentences.zh: 琢磨如何支付预制餐点的费用

sentences.en: and service of women's liberation
sentences.zh: 以及妇女解放的服务，

sentences.en: just wasn't a priority for everyone.
sentences.zh: 对所有人来说根本不是当务之急。

sentences.en: Plus, more private kitchens meant more customers
sentences.zh: 此外，更多私人厨房意味着更多的客户

sentences.en: for electric companies who aggressively marketed their appliances to women.
sentences.zh: 送给那些向女性大肆推销电器的电力公司。

sentences.en: Instead of continuing the additional, taxing, unpaid work of rallying
sentences.zh: 许多女性没有继续从事为争取一个共享、免受劳役之苦的

sentences.en: for a shared, drudgery-free future,
sentences.zh: 未来而奔走的额外、繁重且无报酬的工作，

sentences.en: many women settled for a dishwashing machine.
sentences.zh: 而是满足于一台洗碗机。

sentences.en: The dream of mainstreaming the kitchen-less house was coming to an end.
sentences.zh: 无厨房住宅走向主流的梦想正走向终结。

sentences.en: But the problem of the kitchen remained.
sentences.zh: 但厨房的问题依然存在。

sentences.en: And that brings us back to Margareta Schuttel-Lahatzky,
sentences.zh: 这就把我们带回了玛格丽特·许特尔-拉哈茨基，

sentences.en: the Austrian architect from the beginning of our story.
sentences.zh: 我们故事开头提到的那位奥地利建筑师。

sentences.en: In the 1920s, a young Schuttel-Lahatzky took a very different approach to the home kitchen.
sentences.zh: 20世纪20年代，年轻的许特尔-拉哈茨基对家庭厨房采取了截然不同的方法。

sentences.en: She didn't want to eliminate it.
sentences.zh: 她并不想消灭它。

sentences.en: She wanted to elevate it with clever and scientifically informed design.
sentences.zh: 她希望通过巧妙且符合科学的设计来提升它。

sentences.en: She wanted kitchen work to move with the ease and quickness of a factory
sentences.zh: 她希望厨房工作能像工厂一样轻松快捷地进行，

sentences.en: so women could get in and out and on with their lives beyond the kitchen.
sentences.zh: 这样女性就能进出迅速，去过厨房之外的生活。

sentences.en: Schuttel-Lahatzky's early work in public housing
sentences.zh: 许特尔-拉哈茨基早期在公共住房方面的工作

sentences.en: attracted the attention of city planners in Frankfurt, Germany.
sentences.zh: 吸引了德国法兰克福城市规划师的注意。

sentences.en: They were working on an ambitious government program
sentences.zh: 他们当时正致力于一项雄心勃勃的政府计划，

sentences.en: to overhaul the way that residents of Frankfurt
sentences.zh: 旨在彻底改革法兰克福居民在一战后

sentences.en: lived in the years after World War I.
sentences.zh: 数年里的生活方式。

sentences.en: At the time, many Germans faced immense shortages of almost everything,
sentences.zh: 当时，许多德国人几乎面临着样样紧缺的巨大困境，

sentences.en: including food, fuel, and crucially, housing.
sentences.zh: 包括食物、燃料，以及至关重要的住房。

sentences.en: In Frankfurt, people were living in old tenement buildings
sentences.zh: 在法兰克福，人们住在老旧的廉租公寓里，

sentences.en: or sometimes just in garden plots.
sentences.zh: 有时甚至只住在花园地块里。

sentences.en: So the city government stepped in with an architectural agenda.
sentences.zh: 于是市政府带着一套建筑规划介入了。

sentences.en: It was called the New Frankfurt.
sentences.zh: 这被称为“新法兰克福”。

sentences.en: For the architects of the New Frankfurt, the question really becomes,
sentences.zh: 对于“新法兰克福”的建筑师来说，真正的问题变成了：

sentences.en: how can we create good housing for a large amount of people in a short amount of time?
sentences.zh: 我们如何在短时间内为大量人口建造良好的住房？

sentences.en: S.E.
sentences.zh: S.E.

sentences.en: Eisterer is an assistant professor at Princeton.
sentences.zh: 艾斯特雷尔是普林斯顿大学的助理教授。

sentences.en: She's currently working on a biography of Margareta Schuttel-Lahatzky.
sentences.zh: 她目前正在撰写一本关于玛格丽特·许特尔-拉哈茨基的传记。

sentences.en: And she says to answer that question,
sentences.zh: 她说为了回答这个问题，

sentences.en: the architects of the New Frankfurt took a novel approach.
sentences.zh: “新法兰克福”的建筑师们采取了一种新颖的方法。

sentences.en: They looked to mass production.
sentences.zh: 他们将目光投向了大规模生产。

sentences.en: The idea becomes, how can we use prefabricated elements like walls,
sentences.zh: 这个想法变成了：我们如何利用墙壁等预制构件，

sentences.en: but in some cases also entire room units,
sentences.zh: 但在某些情况下甚至利用整个房间单元，

sentences.en: to produce housing stock quickly?
sentences.zh: 来快速生产房屋库存？

sentences.en: For the first time ever, the German government encouraged the shells of buildings
sentences.zh: 德国政府有史以来第一次鼓励建筑外壳

sentences.en: and sometimes entire rooms, fixtures and all,
sentences.zh: 有时甚至是整个房间及固定装置等，

sentences.en: to be assembled in a factory by machines
sentences.zh: 在工厂里由机器组装，

sentences.en: and then set down on the construction site by crane.
sentences.zh: 然后用起重机放置在施工现场。

sentences.en: These new mass-produced apartments needed cheap and compact kitchens.
sentences.zh: 这些新的量产公寓需要便宜且紧凑的厨房。

sentences.en: And for that, the director of the New Frankfurt project tapped Schuttel-Lahatzky.
sentences.zh: 为此，“新法兰克福”项目负责人找到了许特尔-拉哈茨基。

sentences.en: And she began by studying kitchens on trains and ships.
sentences.zh: 她从研究火车和轮船上的厨房开始入手。

sentences.en: They were obviously wonderful models for efficiency because they didn't have much space.
sentences.zh: 它们显然是提高效率的极佳模范，因为它们空间有限。

sentences.en: And space was expensive.
sentences.zh: 而空间是很昂贵的。

sentences.en: That's Mary McLeod again.
sentences.zh: 那是玛丽·麦克劳德再次发话。

sentences.en: And she says that Schuttel-Lahatzky came up with all of these thoughtful,
sentences.zh: 她说许特尔-拉哈茨基为她的厨房设计想出了所有这些体贴、

sentences.en: practical, and super space-saving touches for her kitchen design.
sentences.zh: 实用且极度节省空间的巧思。

sentences.en: Designs I got to see firsthand when I visited that kitchen in the museum.
sentences.zh: 这些设计是我参观博物馆里的那个厨房时亲眼看到的。

sentences.en: Like a Murphy bed-style, fold-down ironing board.
sentences.zh: 比如墨菲床风格的折叠式熨衣板。

sentences.en: Or this thing called the cookbox, which is kind of like today's crockpot,
sentences.zh: 或者这个叫烹饪盒的东西，有点像今天的慢炖锅，

sentences.en: except it just used residual heat from the stove to slow cook meats or grains or whatever else.
sentences.zh: 只不过它只是利用炉子的余热来慢炖肉类、谷物或其他东西。

sentences.en: And one of my favorite features, these 12 identical measuring cups with spouts
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的特色之一是这12个带有倾倒口的相同量杯，

sentences.en: that fit into cubby holes on the wall,
sentences.zh: 它们可以放入墙上的小方格中，

sentences.en: each labeled with the name of a different grain or foodstuff.
sentences.zh: 每个上面都贴着不同谷物或食品名称的标签。

sentences.en: Those let you measure and pour without dirtying up multiple cups and dishes.
sentences.zh: 这些让你无需弄脏多个杯子和盘子就能进行量取和倾倒。

sentences.en: There were complaints that she didn't have a big enough container for potatoes.
sentences.zh: 有人抱怨她没有准备一个足够大的马铃薯容器。

sentences.en: But for the most part, it was seen as, you know, amazingly efficient.
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，它被认为是非常高效的。

sentences.en: And that efficiency was, of course, by design.
sentences.zh: 这种效率当然是刻意设计的。

sentences.en: Schuttel-Lahatzky was inspired by scientific management,
sentences.zh: 许特尔-拉哈茨基受到科学管理的启发，

sentences.en: a popular idea in the States back in the 1920s.
sentences.zh: 这是20世纪20年代在美国流行的一种思想。

sentences.en: It was mostly applied to factories,
sentences.zh: 它主要应用于工厂，

sentences.en: where managers would obsessively streamline workflows
sentences.zh: 那里的管理者会痴迷于简化工作流程，

sentences.en: in order to theoretically maximize their profits.
sentences.zh: 以便从理论上实现利润最大化。

sentences.en: Schuttel-Lahatzky applied those ideas to the kitchen.
sentences.zh: 许特尔-拉哈茨基将这些理念应用到了厨房中。

sentences.en: And in the interest of minimizing work for so-called housewives,
sentences.zh: 为了尽量减少所谓家庭主妇的劳动，

sentences.en: she did tests to eradicate any excess movements.
sentences.zh: 她通过测试来消除任何多余的动作。

sentences.en: Schuttel-Lahatzky designed so-called motion studies
sentences.zh: 许特尔-拉哈茨基为法兰克福厨房的设计

sentences.en: for the design of the Frankfurt kitchen,
sentences.zh: 设计了所谓的动作研究，

sentences.en: where she mapped intensely what are the shortest paths
sentences.zh: 她深入绘制了在日常烹饪过程中，

sentences.en: between different kitchen elements that you would use
sentences.zh: 你将使用的不同厨房元素之间的

sentences.en: in a regular cooking session, let's say.
sentences.zh: 最短路径是什么。

sentences.en: She tracked women's movements like football plays
sentences.zh: 她像记录橄榄球战术或复杂舞步一样追踪女性的动作，

sentences.en: or complex dance steps with little lines across the floor
sentences.zh: 在地板上画出细线，

sentences.en: and then streamlined accordingly.
sentences.zh: 然后据此进行简化。

sentences.en: In her kitchen, no single step or reach of the arm was unnecessary.
sentences.zh: 在她的厨房里，没有任何一步或一次伸手是多余的。

sentences.en: Women would be like basketball players holding the ball,
sentences.zh: 女性就像持球的篮球运动员一样，

sentences.en: never more than a pivot or step away from where they needed to go.
sentences.zh: 距离她们需要去的地方永远不超过一次转身或一步之遥。

sentences.en: She really just wanted to make women's life easier
sentences.zh: 她真的只是想让女性的生活更轻松，

sentences.en: so they had time for more creative, pleasurable activities
sentences.zh: 好让她们有时间从事更多富有创造力、愉悦的活动

sentences.en: and even intellectual pursuits.
sentences.zh: 甚至是智力追求。

sentences.en: That was the real goal of it.
sentences.zh: 这才是真正的目标。

sentences.en: The Frankfurt kitchen was mass-produced in batches of 10 to 15
sentences.zh: 法兰克福厨房以10到15个为一批进行量产，

sentences.en: with little variations or changes made throughout.
sentences.zh: 其间不断进行微小的调整或改变。

sentences.en: Between 1926 and 1930, the prefab kitchen was installed
sentences.zh: 在1926年至1930年间，这种预制厨房被安装在

sentences.en: in about 10,000 public housing units in Frankfurt
sentences.zh: 法兰克福大约10000套公共住房中，

sentences.en: and architects and public housing leaders across Europe
sentences.zh: 欧洲各地的建筑师和公房领导者

sentences.en: quickly sang its praises.
sentences.zh: 很快对它赞不绝口。

sentences.en: But in practice, this renowned kitchen didn't always jive
sentences.zh: 但在实践中，这个著名的厨房并不总能与人们、女性

sentences.en: with how people, women, actually wanted to use their kitchen.
sentences.zh: 实际想要使用厨房的方式契合。

sentences.en: Sure, there were those complaints that the bin for potatoes was too small,
sentences.zh: 当然，有人抱怨装土豆的容器太小，

sentences.en: but there were bigger issues.
sentences.zh: 但还有更大的问题。

sentences.en: For a long time, kitchens had been integrated into large living rooms
sentences.zh: 长期以来，厨房一直融入在大起居室中，

sentences.en: where people would cook around a big open hearth.
sentences.zh: 人们围着一个大型开放式炉火做饭。

sentences.en: But in the compact New Frankfurt housing,
sentences.zh: 但在紧凑的新法兰克福住宅中，

sentences.en: the kitchen was now separate from other living spaces.
sentences.zh: 厨房现在与其他起居空间分开了。

sentences.en: First, there's work, and that's the kitchen.
sentences.zh: 首先是工作，那就是厨房。

sentences.en: And second, there's living, relaxation, pleasure, free time,
sentences.zh: 其次是生活、放松、快乐、闲暇，

sentences.en: and that's the living room.
sentences.zh: 那就是起居室。

sentences.en: That sounds pretty good in theory.
sentences.zh: 这在理论上听起来很不错。

sentences.en: Leave the drudgery behind you when you close the kitchen door.
sentences.zh: 当你关上厨房门时，就把繁重的工作抛在脑后。

sentences.en: But for many women, household labor was so gendered
sentences.zh: 但对许多女性而言，家务劳动带有强烈的性别色彩

sentences.en: that they also had kids to take care of.
sentences.zh: 以至于她们还得照顾孩子。

sentences.en: Those joint living room kitchens of old,
sentences.zh: 过去那种联排的起居室厨房，

sentences.en: with the big open hearths and the slapped-together furniture,
sentences.zh: 有着巨大的开放式壁炉和拼凑出来的家具，

sentences.en: they may have been slipshod,
